clue.text: Punched by employee, bound to be arrested?

indicators.note: by places the employee piece beside the punched piece

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
cuffed means struck with the hand

explanation.surface: A worker gets hit and seems destined for arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: someone in cuffs is bound, as anyone being arrested is likely to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Police restrain an arrested suspect with cuffs on the wrists, so they are tied up that way.

clue.text: Troubles go missing in drunken hangouts

indicators.note: missing says two letters drop out, and drunken says the rest of the bars word is reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Problems vanish in boozy bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GO from HANGOUTS and rearrange the rest, signalled by 'missing' and 'drunken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that troubles you keeps returning to disturb you, as a ghost does a house.

clue.text: The wild character

definitions.meaning: the natural world untouched by people
a person's basic temperament or disposition

explanation.surface: A short phrase about untamed temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: The untamed outdoors is the natural world, and one's innate temperament is one's essential make-up.

clue.text: Gather I have no one French in family, for instance

parts.note: to gather is to collect
I've is the contraction of I have
un is French for one

explanation.surface: Someone gathers they have no French relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A word like 'family' names a group of individuals as a single unit, which is a grammar term for words such as flock.

clue.text: One sells food Tue-Fri for cooking, with arrears off and on

indicators.note: for cooking says the day abbreviations are mixed up like ingredients
off and on means every other letter of arrears is taken

explanation.surface: A vendor cooks from Tuesday to Friday while paying debts in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' rearranges TUEFRI into FRUITE; 'off and on' takes alternate letters of arrears, giving RER.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengrocer specialising in apples, pears and the like is a trader selling produce.

clue.text: Waterfowl, bottom-up, floundered — I emoted somewhat

indicators.note: bottom-up in a down clue means the hidden letters read from the bottom upwards
somewhat says only part of these words is used, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A duck upended in the water flailed, and the speaker overacted a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' hides REDIE in 'floundered — I emoted'; 'bottom-up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea duck prized for its soft down is a kind of water bird.

clue.text: Tramp's dog's maybe running round

indicators.note: running round says the word for companion animals is turned to read the other way

parts.note: dogs are examples of household animals kept as companions

explanation.surface: A vagrant's dog is perhaps circling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a homeless person; it is the verb to walk heavily. 'running round' turns PETS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk with heavy footfalls, which is to tread or pace.

clue.text: Square cut possibly, with one side going for it

definitions.text: Square cut possibly, with one side going for it

parts.words: Square cut possibly, with one side going for it
parts.note: a four-sided shape sliced corner to corner, or losing a side, ends up as a three-sided figure

explanation.surface: A cricket stroke, the square cut, played by a batsman really going for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The square cut is a cricket shot, but here a square is a shape: cut diagonally, or with a side taken away, it has three sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane shape with three straight sides is what remains when a square is halved diagonally.

clue.text: Claims about nurse seen in part of letter

indicators.note: seen in places the about-and-nurse words within the letter's add-on

parts.note: PS, postscript, is the bit added at the end of a letter
re means about or concerning
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Assertions about a nurse appear in a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend can mean to lay claim to something, as a pretender claims a throne.

clue.text: Motorists may show this forceful lack of inhibition

parts.note: a driving force or driving rain is forceful
licence is freedom from restraint, as in poetic licence

explanation.surface: Drivers display reckless, uninhibited behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver stopped by police must produce the permit that legally allows them on the road.

clue.text: Ruins trifle — odd ingredients should have been discarded before

indicators.text: odd ingredients should have been discarded
indicators.note: throwing away the odd-numbered letters of the two words leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: A cook complains that a trifle was spoiled by odd ingredients that should have been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mark time up to a point, as in 'not till then' and 'not before then'.

clue.text: Lenin rued revolutionary stress

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at turning things over, so the letters of the two words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: The Bolshevik leader regretted a revolutionary emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' fits Lenin's politics, but it is the signal to rearrange LENIN RUED.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to stress it, as drawing a line beneath words does in writing.

clue.text: Component of refrigerator men transported gives bother

indicators.note: Component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Removal men moving a fridge find it a real nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to harass or trouble them, a stronger form of bothering.

clue.text: In turnover, the Queen pub perhaps earns this?

definitions.text: In turnover, the Queen pub perhaps earns this?

indicators.note: in turnover says the royal letters are turned over to read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen
a pub is one example of a place where events are held

explanation.surface: A pub called The Queen hopes its takings bring in money.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a pub's income is what it earns, and 'turnover' is itself a near-synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Income earned by a business, its takings, is its revenue, much as turnover is.

clue.text: A blockbuster movie is so like an American standard

definitions.text: A blockbuster movie is so like an American standard

parts.words: A blockbuster movie is so like an American standard
parts.note: a big film is full of famous actors, and the US flag and anthem are named for being dotted with stars

explanation.surface: A big Hollywood film resembles a classic American song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a jazz tune; it is a flag, the Star-Spangled Banner, also the US national anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: A film crammed with celebrities is jokingly glittering with stars, exactly as the American flag is.

clue.text: Head first

definitions.meaning: the leader of a school or college

explanation.definitionFit: A school's chief is called this, and as an adjective it means foremost or main.

clue.text: Game one's put down after a couple of drinks

indicators.note: in a down clue, put down after means written below the drinks

parts.note: gin and rum are two spirits
my is what one's means when the speaker talks of themself

explanation.surface: Someone lays down their cards after a couple of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for two in which players form sets and runs is a classic rummy variant.

clue.text: Result comes with player making catch

parts.note: a draw is a result in a match
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A match result arrives as a player takes a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' looks like a fielding act; it is a noun, a hidden snag.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden disadvantage or snag, as in 'what's the catch?'.

clue.text: Like Wham or Bananarama but not Abba or A-ha?

definitions.text: Like Wham or Bananarama but not Abba or A-ha?

parts.words: Like Wham or Bananarama but not Abba or A-ha?
parts.note: Abba and A-ha read the same backwards, while the other two band names do not

explanation.surface: A quiz question sorting 1980s pop acts into two groups.
explanation.walkthrough: The music is a red herring: the test is spelling, since only Abba and A-ha are palindromes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be turned around or undone is permanent, and these band names cannot be read back the same way.

clue.text: Around new hospital, two old boys hang about

indicators.note: around means the old boys sit either side of the new letter
two means the old boy abbreviation is used twice

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Two former pupils loiter around a new hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to socialise or mix familiarly, much like hanging around with people.

clue.text: Mutual admiration ceremonies? You may see one or two in Hollywood

definitions.meaning: film award nights jokingly seen as the industry praising itself

definitions.text: You may see one or two in Hollywood
definitions.meaning: the statuettes are found in Hollywood, and the word Hollywood contains two of the letter O

explanation.surface: A dig at self-congratulatory awards nights in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half also hints at the letter O, which appears twice in Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Awards, Hollywood's annual film prizes, are known by the nickname of their golden statuette.

clue.text: Reels back, seeing Liverpool snatching victory

indicators.note: snatching means the club's nickname grabs the victory word and holds it inside

parts.note: Liverpool FC are nicknamed the Reds from their red shirts
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A football club snatches a win and a fan replays the highlights.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool are an English football club, known as the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding a tape or film back onto its reel is rewinding it.

clue.text: Cut complete broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: sheer means complete or utter, as in sheer nonsense

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut a complete programme being aired.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to clip or cut off, as with sheep's wool.

clue.text: Cushions doubly firm — relative shifting second to back

indicators.note: doubly means the abbreviation for a firm appears twice

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: shifting second to back moves the relative's leading letter, its s, to the end

parts.note: a son is a family relative

explanation.surface: Cushions twice as firm, with a relative shifting the second one to the back of the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting second to back' moves the S of SON to the end, giving ONS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion something is to wrap it protectively, as silk or padding envelops and shelters.

clue.text: A supreme blending with main ingredient from Burgundy — cut the mustard?

indicators.note: blending says the letters are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: the letter u is the one Burgundy holds most of, appearing twice in it

explanation.surface: A rich sauce blended with Burgundy wine, and a question of whether it cuts the mustard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blending' mixes A SUPREME with U, the most frequent letter of Burgundy, so the 'main ingredient' of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is an idiom for meeting the required standard, being good enough.

clue.text: One might assassinate knight in German agreement

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A would-be assassin is a knight with German consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese feudal spies trained in stealth were hired as covert killers.

clue.text: Right in the old harness

indicators.note: in puts the word for right inside the old word

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: An old harness is said to be right.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden crossbar that couples draught animals together for ploughing is a type of harness.

clue.text: Old transporter's role subtly changed

indicators.note: changed means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old vehicle's role has quietly altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subtly' looks like part of the indicator; it is fodder, with 'changed' alone signalling the rearrangement of ROLE SUBTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric buses fed by overhead wires were a common public transport vehicle, now largely gone in Britain.
